title: Hearing Buddy Bolden at Congo Square on a visit
summary: Bolden was on his way out; he heard him and other bands outside Globe Hall at the square.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Do you remember a carnet player, Buddy Bolden? Did he ever get down there on excursion or anything?

Not that I know of. Bolden was on his way out when I got here. I heard him several times. He used to go around by the... He used to have a square right where the auditorium is now. That square that used to go straight across, used to be named Congo Square, the changes to Burgard Square. And they had a hall that's called the Globe Hall right there. Where you could sit down out in the square, when they're going to have a dance there, they'll come outside and play two, three numbers. That's where I heard Bolden, some Manuel Perez, all different bands would come around. They would get out and play a couple of numbers. Franky Dusen.
Did you hear Bolden after you moved up here or did you come up here on a visit sometime before...
Yeah. And he had a couple of pieces he made famous notes that put on record and things like that. Just called them Bolden. So we, our Magnolia band came up here and played, played a parade, you know?
